title: Architecting Real-Time Multimodal AI Systems with Gemini 2.5
overview: A technical keynote exploring modern multimodal architectures, streaming token generation, video-to-knowledge pipelines, and distributed vector indexing.
executive_summary:
In this technical deep dive, the presenter outlines the core paradigms of high-throughput multimodal intelligence. The session highlights how native multimodal models like Gemini 2.5 unify audio, video, OCR, and reasoning into a single inference pass, eliminating cumbersome multi-stage transcription and vision pipelines.

The speaker addresses key architectural bottlenecks, specifically latency reduction during video frame sampling and contextual window utilization for long-form video knowledge extraction. Finally, the talk transitions into practical deployment patterns, including vector retrieval over timestamped embeddings and caching strategies for sub-second enterprise Q&A.
key_takeaways: Native multimodal reasoning reduces latency by 4x compared to chained pipeline architectures (ASR + OCR + LLM).
Timestamped semantic chunking allows precise sub-second video seeking without full re-indexing.
Gemini Files API supports up to 2 million tokens of context, enabling multi-hour lecture extraction.
Cost efficiency is maximized through server-side caching of video context for subsequent Q&A queries.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Sarah Chen
transcript.text: Hello everyone, and welcome to this session on architecting real-time multimodal intelligence. Today we're diving into native video understanding.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Sarah Chen
transcript.text: Historically, processing media required orchestrating whisper models, separate OCR engines, and external embeddings. That era is fundamentally shifting.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Sarah Chen
transcript.text: With Gemini 2.5, we feed raw video streams directly into the model. Visual tokens and audio features are processed in an interleaved attention space.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Sarah Chen
transcript.text: This means you get speech transcription, OCR detection on code editors, and visual motion analysis simultaneously with zero loss of temporal context.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Sarah Chen
transcript.text: By constraining generation with strict Pydantic schemas, we instantly produce chronological chapters and topic maps with exact millisecond bounds.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Sarah Chen
transcript.text: Look at the slide on screen: notice how the latency graph drops from 4.2 seconds down to 850 milliseconds when caching context.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Sarah Chen
transcript.text: For enterprise search, users don't just want text summaries—they want to click a timestamp and jump immediately to the exact explanation.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Sarah Chen
transcript.text: Thank you for joining. All code repositories and interactive dashboards are open sourced in our project repository. Let's build together!
